known.title: A review block that quotes an earlier round opens a block of its own, so the quoted verdict wins
known.summary: parseReviewComment maps every line through `reviewText` (plan.mjs:759), which removes blockquote, list, and emphasis marks, and only then tests each line with REVIEW_BLOCK_HEADING (plan.mjs:750, 764-767) to start a new block. So a passing block that quotes an earlier round (`> ### Code review round 1` followed by `> Code-review: fixes-required`, or the same lines as list items) opens a block of its own, its quoted verdict counts, and the most severe verdict makes the round read as fixes-required (repair for a plan review). The contract text (plan-contract.md:190-196) states the same rule, a block starts at any heading line after the marks are removed. Only an unquoted heading line, `#` after at most three spaces, may start a block.
